location.basis: Located on Esri World Imagery at zoom 16 and 18 from the excavated remains inside the fenced archaeological park on the right bank of the Indus: the coordinates are those of the Buddhist stupa on the western (citadel) mound; the excavated lower-town blocks lie 350-950 m east and south-east of it. The commonly cited site coordinates (about 27.33 N, 68.14 E) fall inside the same park.

structures.description: Exposed brick architecture of the central citadel mound around the Great Bath: the Great Bath complex, the blocks north and east of it, and the western buildings. The stupa and its monastery (Kushan period, not Harappan) are cut out as a hole, and the polygon stops short of the visitor path that enters from the north.
structures.holes_note: hole: the Buddhist stupa and its monastery (Kushan period)
structures.eye_check: Overlay checked by eye: the peak direction runs parallel to the walls of the Great Bath complex and to the deep N-S lane east of it; the western buildings look turned slightly less clockwise (the west half of the polygon peaks lower).

structures.description: Exposed architecture of the southern citadel excavations, about 300 m south of the stupa: a western building, a building with rows of square piers (possibly the pillared hall of the published plans) and a southern building. The diagonal visitor path north of the buildings and the path to the south-east are outside the polygon.
structures.eye_check: Overlay checked by eye: the peak follows the pier rows and the southern building; the western building is turned further clockwise (its north wall S11), which produces the shoulder above the main peak.

structures.description: Northern excavated block of the lower town, about 370 m east and 185 m north of the stupa, including the long E-W street that crosses it and a small western annex. The visitor path that enters the block from the west along the street line, and the straight cleared band along the east side of the block (a visitor path that continues south through unexcavated ground), are excluded.
structures.holes_note: hole: visitor path entering from the west along the street line
structures.eye_check: Overlay checked by eye: the peak follows the E-W street and the long N-S walls of both halves of the block; the secondary peaks are weak (15 percent of the main peak) and come from sand ripples and tree shadows, not from walls.

structures.description: North part of the south-central lower-town block, about 330 m east and 220 m south of the stupa. Low-relief walls partly covered by sand, with a tree shadow cut out as a hole.
structures.eye_check: Overlay checked by eye: the histogram is a plateau without a clear single peak, and the walls are faint. We do not consider the automatic value reliable here; the one check line and the adjacent south-east part (P4b) suggest a direction within the range of the other lower-town blocks.

structures.description: South-east part of the south-central lower-town block, west of the diagonal visitor path that runs N-S along its east side (excluded).
structures.eye_check: Overlay checked by eye: the peak follows the E-W and N-S walls of the small houses; a secondary peak near the value of the northern block is also present.

structures.description: Southern excavated lower-town block, about 330 m east and 420 m south of the stupa, with a broad N-S street through its eastern third and house blocks on both sides. The modern E-W path to the north and the paths along the southern edge are outside the polygon.
structures.eye_check: Overlay checked by eye: the peak follows the E-W walls and the street edges. The broad N-S street is not perfectly straight: its northern stretch (S36, S38) is turned further clockwise than its southern stretch (S31, S33).

structures.description: Eastern lower-town block, about 1 km east of the stupa: low-relief walls of several houses in scrub.
structures.eye_check: Overlay checked by eye: the walls are faint and the histogram is broad with several peaks; the automatic value is of low reliability and changes with the analysis parameters by several degrees.

structures.description: Union of the five lower-town polygons P3, P4, P4b, P5 and P6, measured as one area to give a single lower-town direction; resampling uses 60 m blocks so that the error reflects differences between neighbouring blocks.
structures.eye_check: Dominated by the two largest and clearest blocks (P3, P5); the peak lies between their individual peaks.

systems.note: Combined lower-town measurement; the check lines are listed under the individual blocks.

main_system_reason: The town's main layout is the street-and-house grid of the lower town. sys7 measures all exposed lower-town architecture at once; the two blocks that dominate it (sys3, the northern block with the longest continuous street, and sys5, the southern block with the broad N-S street) have the sharpest and most stable peaks. The citadel (sys1, sys2) is reported separately as a different part.
notes: Esri World Imagery at zoom 18 (0.53 m per pixel; the service reports a 0.34 m Vantor Vivid image of 31 January 2025, published to zoom 18 only). The excavated Harappan brickwork is clearly visible in five lower-town blocks and in two excavated areas of the citadel mound; the rest of the mound surface is scrub and trees. We did not identify the excavators' area names (HR, VS, DK and others) from the imagery, so the parts are named by position. Modern and later features excluded: the stupa and monastery (a Kushan building on the citadel), visitor paths (one runs as a straight cleared band along the east side of the northern block and continues south through unexcavated ground, and could be mistaken for a long N-S street), the perimeter road and fence, and site buildings in the north-west. Within each block the individual walls scatter by a few degrees about the automatic peak, and neighbouring blocks differ from one another by up to about 6 degrees, so the town is better described by its block values than by one number. The eastern block (P6) and the north part of the south-central block (P4) give unreliable automatic values.
